## Overview

A UBC MDS Capstone project predicting patient mortality and hospital
readmission at 1, 6, and 12 months post-discharge by combining 3D CT
imaging with structured electronic health record (EHR) data, in partnership
with Tandem Research.

The primary deliverable is a reproducible ML pipeline with full
explainability — so clinicians and future data scientists can understand
not just what the model predicts, but which patient features drive those
predictions.

---

## The Problem

Clinicians currently lack reliable tools to identify which patients are at
highest risk of death or readmission after a pulmonary embolism diagnosis.
Most medical AI models use either tabular EHR data or 3D imaging — rarely
both. This project aims to close that gap.

---

## Dataset

The [INSPECT dataset](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2311.10798), curated by
Stanford Research — 23,248 CTPA (CT pulmonary angiography) studies from
19,402 patients, integrating 3D imaging with longitudinal EHR data.

---

## Approach

We replicate and extend an existing late-fusion multimodal architecture as
a baseline, then propose a cascaded approach that introduces imaging-derived
signals earlier in the pipeline so the EHR model can learn interactions
between imaging findings and structured clinical data directly.

Both approaches include SHAP-based explainability to identify the most
influential clinical variables per prediction task.

---

## Explainability

Feature importance analyses will be generated for all model components
across all prediction tasks, identifying the most influential clinical variables
per task. Two concrete deliverables are required for partner sign-off:

- A feature importance report summarizing which EHR features drive each prediction
- Confirmation that outputs are clinically meaningful and interpretable by a
  non-technical clinician

---

## Success Criteria

- **AUROC ≥ 0.90** across all prediction horizons on the held-out test set
- **AUPRC ≥ 0.50** to demonstrate robust performance despite class imbalance
- Full pipeline reproducible from a single command in the GitHub repository
- Partner sign-off on clinical interpretability
